fields.features_heading: Cells, Screeners, and Quotas From One Prompt
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the concept testing survey, the logic that decides who sees which concept, and the database behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Drafted from your concept boards

Describe each concept in a sentence or paste the copy people see. Emergent drafts a screen for each one and the questions that follow it, and a follow-up prompt edits any of them.
fields.feature_2:
One concept per person, or all of them

Ask for a monadic design and the app shows each person one concept, split evenly across cells. Ask for sequential and it shows every concept, in a new random order each time.
fields.feature_3:
A screener that ends the survey early

Put the qualifying questions first, like a purchase in the past 30 days. Anyone outside the target sees a short thank-you screen, and their row is saved with a screened-out status.
fields.feature_4:
Each answer saved with its concept and cell

Every response is a row in a database you own, tagged with the concept shown, its cell, and its position in the order. Compare the share who would buy across cells from one table.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a cell reaches its quota

Set a quota for each cell, such as 100 qualified answers. The app emails your insights lead or posts in a Slack channel once a cell fills, and stops sending new people to that cell.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, exported on paid plans

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, then run the next round of concepts on the same build, with every earlier round still sitting in your tables.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Concept Tests, Four Go or No-Go Calls
fields.tab_content_1:
Design B wins its cell with 92 of 200

Brightfield Granola had 3 package designs and one question: which would sell? The survey showed each of 600 shoppers a single design, 200 per cell. No one compared designs side by side. In the Design B cell, 92 of 200 said they would definitely or probably buy. Design A drew 68 of 200 and Design C 58.
fields.tab_content_2:
In random order, shared calendars rate 4.2 of 5

Tallyroot asked 320 customers to rate the appeal of 4 feature concepts from 1 to 5. Each customer saw all 4 in a new random order. No concept always came first. Shared calendars averaged 4.2 and offline mode 3.8. Invoice templates (3.3) and team chat (2.7) fell under the 3.5 line for the roadmap shortlist.
fields.tab_content_3:
Tobin hears when both cells fill to 100

Hearthpaw Pet Foods wanted only people who bought dog food in the past 30 days. Of 412 who started, 200 passed the screener and 212 ended early. Each qualified person saw one concept, fresh-frozen or grain-free, up to 100 per cell. When both cells reached 100, the app emailed insights lead Tobin Achterberg.
fields.tab_content_4:
Downtown and Riverside split on the cold brew

Ferngate Coffee Roasters has no customer email list. It put a survey link at the counter of 2 stores instead. Customers answered on their phones, one question per screen, about a new oat milk cold brew. Over one weekend, 137 answered. At Downtown, 38 of 73 said they would buy it. At Riverside, 20 of 64 did.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Concept Testing Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a concept testing survey that shows each concept fairly and points to the one worth taking forward.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write each concept as one screen
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose one concept or all per person
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put the screener before any concept
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give each concept a name, a two-line description, an image if you have one, and a price only when price is part of the idea. Keep every concept the same length. A longer description can win on detail alone.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Show one concept per person when your sample can fill a cell for each, and every answer reads as a first impression. With a smaller sample, show every concept to each person and ask Emergent to shuffle the order per respondent.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask the qualifying questions first: whether the person buys the category, how recently, and who they buy for. Set the answer that ends the survey for anyone outside the target, and keep their rows to count how many qualified.
fields.howto_step_4_des: After every concept, ask the same questions in the same order: how likely they are to buy on a 5-point scale, overall appeal, how new it feels, and how believable it is. Close with one open question on what they would change.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set a quota for every cell
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide how many qualified answers each cell needs before launch, such as 100 or 200, and put the number in your prompt. The app stops sending people to a full cell and emails you when the last cell fills.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Pilot with 5 people from the target
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the draft to 5 people who would pass your screener. Ask which concept screen they read twice and where they stopped. Fix those screens with a follow-up prompt before the link goes to your full panel or customer list.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the cells side by side
fields.howto_step_7_des: Compare the share who would definitely or probably buy in each cell, then read the open answers for the top 2 concepts. Pick the one to take forward, and leave the others in the table for the next round.

faq_plan.q: What is a concept testing survey?
faq_plan.a: A concept testing survey shows people a product or ad idea before launch and records how they react: whether they would buy it and what they would change. Concept testing is an early-stage market research method, run before money goes into building the idea.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a concept testing survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the concepts, the people you want to hear from, and the questions to ask after each concept in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder. Emergent builds the survey, the screener and cell logic, and a database for every answer. Try it with a few people from your target, then send the link to your panel or customer list.

faq_plan.q: What are good concept testing survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Good ones use plain wording and a fixed answer scale for each question. After every concept, ask how likely the person is to buy it, how different it is from what they buy now, and how believable its main claim is. Add a price question only when the concept shows a price, and keep the wording identical across concepts.

faq_plan.q: What are some concept testing survey examples?
faq_plan.a: Here are four. A package test shows each shopper one of 3 designs. A feature test has customers rate 4 ideas in random order. A tagline test checks ad copy, and a counter test asks coffee customers about a new drink. Each asks about something that does not exist yet, unlike a wellness survey, which tracks habits people already have. Swap in your own concepts in the prompt.

faq_plan.q: How many respondents do concept testing surveys need per concept?
faq_plan.a: Plan for at least 100 qualified answers per cell, and 200 if you want to compare groups such as regions inside a cell. In a monadic test that number applies to each concept: 3 concepts at 200 each means 600 people. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and the cell size is limited only by the people you can reach.

faq_plan.q: Should a concept testing survey be monadic or sequential monadic?
faq_plan.a: Pick monadic if you can reach enough people to give every concept its own group, and sequential monadic if you cannot. In a monadic test, respondents complete a full evaluation of a single concept. In a sequential monadic test, respondents complete full evaluations for multiple concepts, and the order of concepts is randomized to reduce the odds of bias.

faq_plan.q: How is a concept testing survey different from a broader study of the market?
faq_plan.a: A concept testing survey answers one narrow question: how do people react to this specific idea? A market research survey covers the market around it, such as who buys in the category and why they switch brands. Run the broader study first to find the gap, then a concept test to check the idea that fills it.

faq_plan.q: Who should a concept testing survey screen out?
faq_plan.a: Screen out anyone who has not bought in the category in the past 90 days, plus anyone who works in market research or for a competing brand. Screening questions help ensure respondents fit the target audience of the concept. Put them before any concept appears. Screened-out rows stay in a database you own, which shows how many people on your list qualified.

faq_plan.q: How do I read concept testing survey results?
faq_plan.a: Start with the share in each cell who picked the top two answers on the purchase question, and compare shares rather than raw counts. Then check appeal and believability for the top 2 concepts, and read the open answers for what to fix. A concept that feels new but scores low on believability needs clearer proof before it goes further.

faq_plan.q: Does a needs assessment come before a concept testing survey?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when you do not yet know which problem to solve. A needs assessment survey asks people what they lack or struggle with, and a concept test then checks whether your answer to that gap lands. Emergent builds both from a prompt, and the concept test can reuse the screener from the first study.

plan.angle: The top 10 are guides (Qualtrics, Maze, Appinio, Lyssna, Drive Research) and question lists (Formbricks, SmartSurvey) that explain monadic and sequential monadic designs but leave the reader to build the cells, the screener and the quotas by hand. This page is the concept testing survey itself: four tests built from a prompt, each ending in a go or no-go read (a monadic package test with one design per cell, a sequential test of 4 feature concepts in random order, a screener with quotas that emails the insights lead when both cells fill, and a phone test at two coffee counters split by store), with the FAQ covering which questions to ask, sample size per cell, monadic versus sequential, and how to read the results. Broad market sizing belongs to the market research survey sibling.
